t: Indian independence movement: India became a republic under a new constitution, with Rajendra Prasad as president and Jawaharlal Nehru as prime minister.

In a trial lasting less than 90 minutes, German–British physicist Klaus Fuchs was convicted of violating the Official Secrets Act by supplying information from the Manhattan Project to the Soviet Union.
Scientists at Lawrence Berkeley National Laboratory announced the synthesis of californium, a radioactive transuranium element.
Usmar Ismail began shooting Darah dan Doa, widely recognised as the first Indonesian film.
Gwendolyn Brooks became the first African American to receive the Pulitzer Prize for Poetry.
The Tollund Man, a naturally mummified corpse, was discovered in a peat bog near Silkeborg, Denmark.
Maurice Herzog and Louis Lachenal, members of the French Annapurna expedition, became the first climbers to reach the summit of a peak higher than 8,000 metres (26,247 ft) above sea level.
Thomas Blamey became the only Australian to attain the rank of field marshal.
The Korean War began with North Korean forces launching a pre-dawn raid over the 38th parallel into South Korea.
The United Nations Security Council passed Resolution 82 condemning the North Korean invasion of South Korea.
A Douglas DC-4 Skymaster aircraft crashed after departing from Perth, becoming the worst peacetime aviation accident in Australia's history.
Korean War: Five North Korean aircraft attacked an American air convoy above Suwon Air Base in the first air engagement of the Korean War.
Korean War: South Korean forces began the Bodo League massacre, summarily executing tens of thousands of suspected North Korean sympathizers.
The United States defeated England during the FIFA World Cup in one of the greatest upsets in the competition's history.
Korean War: In the first encounter between North Korean and American forces, an unprepared and undisciplined U.S. Army task force was routed at the Battle of Osan.
Korean War: American troops withdrew from Cheonan, in modern-day South Korea, after suffering heavy casualties from a North Korean attack.
Korean War: North Korean troops began attacking the headquarters of the American 24th Infantry Division in present-day Daejeon, South Korea.
Korean War: A Korean People's Army unit massacred 31 prisoners of war of the U.S. Army on a mountain near the village of Tuman.
Uruguay won the decisive match of the fourth FIFA World Cup, defeating Brazil 2–1 at the Maracanã Stadium in Rio de Janeiro.
Korean War: After a month-long campaign, much of the North Korean air force was destroyed by United Nations forces.
Korean War: After American troops withdrew, North Korean forces captured the village of Yongdong in South Korea.

Korean War: Over fears that North Korean soldiers were infiltrating refugee columns, U.S. forces concluded a four-day massacre of hundreds of civilians through shootings and air attacks near the village of Nogeun-ri.
At the height of a political crisis known as the royal question, four workers were shot dead by the Belgian Gendarmerie at a strike in Grâce-Berleur.
Korean War: Forty-two American prisoners of war were massacred by the Korean People's Army on a hill above Waegwan, South Korea.
The 766th Independent Infantry Regiment of North Korea was disbanded after fighting for less than two months in the Korean War.
Korean War: United Nations forces repelled an attempt by North Korea to capture the city of Taegu.
American tennis player Althea Gibson became the first African-American woman to compete at the U.S. National Championships.
Korean War: The Korean People's Army retreated from the Battle of the Pusan Perimeter after six weeks of fighting, marking the farthest that the KPA would advance in the war.
Korean War: A North Korean attack was repelled by Allied forces at the Battle of Nam River.

The "Great Smoke Pall", generated by the Chinchaga fire, the largest recorded fire in North American history, was first recorded in present-day Nunavut and may eventually have circled the entire globe.

A field-sequential color system developed by Hungarian-American engineer Peter Goldmark became the first color television system to be adopted for commercial use, only for it to be abandoned a year later.
CBS's field-sequential color system for television was the first to be licensed for broadcast by the U.S. Federal Communications Commission.
The first novel of the The Chronicles of Narnia series by C. S. Lewis, The Lion, the Witch and the Wardrobe, was published in the United Kingdom.

The People's Volunteer Army ambushed the South Korean II Corps at the Battle of Onjong, and elsewhere engaged the 1st Infantry Division at the Battle of Unsan, marking China's entry into the Korean War.
Korean War: The 27th British Commonwealth Brigade succeeded in preventing a Chinese breakthrough at the Battle of Pakchon.
The 14th Dalai Lama assumed full temporal power as ruler of Tibet at the age of 15.
Two trains collided near Valemount, Canada, killing 21 people.
Korean War: The Chinese People's Volunteer Army launched multiple attacks against United Nations forces, beginning the Battle of Chosin Reservoir.
Korean War: UN forces began a retreat from North Korea following defeat at the Battle of the Ch'ongch'on River.
Korean War: North Korean troops attacked United Nations forces in the first of two battles at Wonju.
